findings.body:
**Use distinct exception classes in the CLI refusal test.**

At `apps/crq-python/test_deploy_controller_unit_switch.py`, Line 919, each iteration assigns the same exception class to all three binding attributes. A handler that catches only `LiveBindingRefused` can therefore pass the `FactoryRefused` and `CompletionError` cases too. Define three distinct classes, keep all three bound in every iteration, and vary only the class that `production_adapter` raises.
findings.title: Use distinct exception classes in the CLI refusal test.

findings.body:
**Make the retained source commit differ from live HEAD.**

At `apps/crq-python/test_deploy_controller_unit_switch.py`, Line 798, `pending_record()` captures the current checkout. The checkout does not change before recovery. The assertion therefore also passes if recovery sends live HEAD to the factory instead of the retained SHA. Use two distinct valid fixture commits at the factory boundary and assert that it receives the journal’s SHA.
findings.title: Make the retained source commit differ from live HEAD.

findings.body:
**Check that recovery fences the unit before retrying release.**

At `apps/crq-python/test_deploy_controller_unit_switch.py`, Line 233, the first release has already set `running=True` before it crashes. Recovery could skip `stop_and_drain`, call `restore_activation` again, and still satisfy every assertion in this test. Record the recovery drain and the second release. Assert that the drain occurs first.
findings.title: Check that recovery fences the unit before retrying release.

findings.body:
**Assert that the lock context propagates the caller’s exception.**

At `apps/crq-python/test_deploy_controller_unit_switch.py`, Line 1046, a `RuntimeError` raised before the context manager yields satisfies the assertion. That skips the in-block contention check. If the failed acquisition leaves the file unlocked and unchanged, the remaining checks also pass. Create the exception before entering the context, raise it inside the block, and assert that the caught exception is that same object.
findings.title: Assert that the lock context propagates the caller’s exception.

findings.body:
**Check sibling ownership in the queue after preparation.**

At Line 106, `original` retains the pre-call dictionary. If `prepare_current_job` replaces the queue entry with a stale run or one that omits F2, both assertions still pass. Read `old-run` from `self.queue` after preparation and assert its state and sibling membership there.
findings.title: Check sibling ownership in the queue after preparation.

findings.body:
**Reload the persisted queue before replaying the sibling outcome.**

After the injected write failure, this test reuses the same in-memory queue. It passes if harvest marks the run failed only in memory, even though a fresh tick would reload the earlier state. Save the two-job fixture before injecting the failure. Then reload `state/queue.json`, assert the terminal run is present, and replay against the reloaded item.
findings.title: Reload the persisted queue before replaying the sibling outcome.

findings.body:
**Assert that bounded CLI dispatch does not enumerate the inbox.**

An implementation that lists the entire inbox and then dispatches `[job]` still passes this test. The corrupt-file case at Line 235 checks that the direct selector does not parse an unrelated file, not that the CLI avoids listing it. Guard the inbox-listing operation in this test and keep the existing dispatch and JSON assertions.
findings.title: Assert that bounded CLI dispatch does not enumerate the inbox.

findings.body:
**Isolate the fixer size and anchor refusals.**

Changing `job['finding']['body']` leaves both finding digests bound to the original body. Because the test accepts any `ValueError`, stale-binding rejection can satisfy the assertions even if size or anchor validation is broken. Recompute both digests for each case, assert the intended rejection, and verify that a small body with `2: pinned code` reaches the mocked command under the same config.
findings.title: Isolate the fixer size and anchor refusals.

findings.body:
**Recover from the last successful write and verify publication replay.**

If the publication queue write fails, the earlier terminal queue write has already succeeded. At `test_review_admission_execution.py:487–490`, the test discards that saved state and calls `finish()`, which disables publication. The assertions can pass even if replay from the saved terminal state is broken. Restore the last successful queue snapshot, enable publication during recovery, and assert that replay retains one event without duplicating the outbox entry. Give each case its own receipt and outbox directories so only artifacts written by that case survive its simulated crash.
findings.title: Recover from the last successful write and verify publication replay.

findings.body:
**Assert that each selected persistence failure occurred.**

At `test_review_admission_execution.py:481–484`, the test accepts any `OSError` and also accepts no error. If completion bypasses the selected fault injection, the test can still pass after the fresh completion at Line 490. Assert that the selected injection fired. Then check the expected exception or handled failure state before starting recovery.
findings.title: Assert that each selected persistence failure occurred.

findings.body:
**Check the launch reservation for the current generation.**

At `test_review_admission_execution.py:563`, `saved` contains writes from every generation. Generation 1's `launch_pending` record can satisfy the assertion for generations 2 and 3 even if they never persist a reservation. Match the saved item ID and run ID to the current launch, and require that write to occur before its `Popen` call.
findings.title: Check the launch reservation for the current generation.

findings.body:
**Isolate the real planner calls from the caller's Git environment.**

At `test_review_admission_execution.py:409`, the real planner calls `crq.git` without an explicit environment. If the caller exports `GIT_DIR` for another repository, setting `CLONE` changes the working directory but does not change which repository Git opens. `merge-base` then fails if that repository lacks the fixture head. The fixture's own Git helper already strips these overrides. Apply the same isolation to the test's real `crq.git` calls so the planner and timeout tests still exercise the production wrapper. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Isolate the real planner calls from the caller's Git environment.

findings.body:
**Check exact QEMU resource arguments.**

The joined-string assertions pass for `-m 20480` and `-smp 20`. This test would accept ten times the expected memory and vCPU counts. Assert that the tokens following `-m` and `-smp` are exactly `2048` and `2`.
findings.title: Check exact QEMU resource arguments.

findings.body:
**Require the complete set of evidence checks.**

`test_all_checks_proven` iterates only over keys that `build_checks` returns. If a regression drops a required check, this test does not examine it. Even an empty mapping passes this loop. Assert the expected keys independently of `build_checks`, then check their values.
findings.title: Require the complete set of evidence checks.

findings.body:
**Check a failed stop with a successful empty job query.**

Every case that expects `queued_stop_proven` to be false here also leaves the fixture job waiting. A verifier that ignores the stop return code still passes. Add a case with `stop_queued_fixture.rc == 1` and `jobs2_after_stop == self._jobs()`. Keep the successful-stop case with the job still waiting.
findings.title: Check a failed stop with a successful empty job query.

findings.body:
**Test the two queue setup requirements separately.**

This case fails `queue_start` and removes the waiting fixture in the same input. The assertion still passes if `build_checks` stops enforcing either requirement. Test a failed start with the waiting fixture present, and a successful start without the waiting fixture. Both cases must leave `queued_setup_proven` false.
findings.title: Test the two queue setup requirements separately.

findings.body:
**Mock `systemctl` in the mismatched-process refusal test.**

If the ownership check in `process_matches` stops rejecting a mismatched start time, `stop_owned_process` runs `systemctl --user stop crq-vm-test.scope` with no mock. It then polls the test runner's own PID for up to 30 seconds. The test does not kill that PID directly. Its only host effect is the `systemctl` call on the fixed scope name. Patch `subprocess.run` in this test and assert that it is not called.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-            with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
-                vm.stop_owned_process(
-                    {"run_id": "r1", "path": str(run)}, purge=False)
+            with mock.patch.object(vm.subprocess, "run") as run_cmd:
+                with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
+                    vm.stop_owned_process(
+                        {"run_id": "r1", "path": str(run)}, purge=False)
+            run_cmd.assert_not_called()
```

</details>
findings.title: Mock `systemctl` in the mismatched-process refusal test.
